entry.title: LizstarTrek - Lower Decks Season 4
entry.content:
Every Sunday my Twitch subs and I watch Star Trek in my Discord. Here are my reviews and thoughts on each of the episodes as I see it. If you’re curious about a nerd’s views on Star Trek episodes, please read on, I go quite in depth with some of these episodes! I’ve watched some Star Trek before but not all of it!

I know very little about this show except it was made by nerds like me with a very different sense of humor. God, please be good. The last season was really good!! So maybe this’ll be even better?!

Twovix - ENT 8.5/10

New season, new member of the crew! T’Lyn is here. She’s funny.

Boimler is told that as long as he doesn’t do something historically significantly bad, he’s going to be promoted to Lieutenant Jr. Grade. Welp. Sucks to be you, Boimler. The ship goes to the Neutral Zone to find out that they’re going to be transporting Voyager to Starfleet so it’ll become a museum.

Unfortunately, right as they’re about to head out, Billups and T’Ana get fused in the same way Tuvix did. The captain is like “well don’t worry, Janeway solved this, let me look just look up what she- what the FUCK?!”

Honestly the fact that they even bring this up is hilarious. It’s like pissing on the third rail. Tuvix is one of the most divisive things ever. They of course go “no, I won’t kill them, wtf, let’s go fix them” but they look up what happened to Tuvix and decide “I WILL NOT BE TAKEN OUT LIKE THIS. I’LL JUST TURN EVERYONE INTO A TUVIX.

Woah, bird captain is hot.

Meanwhile on Voyager, things get out of hand cause a macrovirus gets loose and gets borg’d. Boimler can fix it but doesn’t, why? Cause he’s anxious about his promotion. Not cause he doesn’t wanna fuck it up but cause he doesn’t WANT to be promoted. But after a pep talk from Mariner, he fixes it all. Well, Rutherford fixes it by gunking it up with cheese.

T’Lyn “fixes” the problem by just teleporting everyone into a holding cell, turning them into… this. This might be the most horrifying thing in all of Star Trek. Tendi fixes it with some quick thinking, thankfully.

In celebration of everyone fixing the day, everyone is promoted to Lt. Jr Class. Except Rutherford, cause he technically broke stuff. Even Mariner gets promoted, which she is very VERY UNHAPPY ABOUT.

Then the episode ends with Ma’ah. Remember him? He’s the Klingon from a while ago, the first real good episode IMO. He and his bird of prey come across some enemy ship that powers down their shields and weapons and are immediately blasted out of space. Oooh, setup for something else :o

I Have No Bones, Yet I Must Flee - ENT 10/10

Absolutely amazing title, holy shit.

The episode starts with some random Romulan ship getting blasted by the random ship from last episode. Every Star Trek season needs some giant arc that’s galaxy threatening, huh??

Holy shit. This is amazing out of context. Anyways Mariner hears Ransom talk about how she’s “not going to be his problem” for long, so she decides to just be a shithead all day so she’s demoted on her own terms. Meanwhile, Rutherford decides to work as hard as he can so he’ll be promoted today. That’s sure to not backfire. Both of these plans. Rutherford’s plan is immediately stunted cause The New Guy, Livik, is stealing his thunder

LOL Boimler’s new room is right in front of the nacelle so it’s super bright. Thats really funny. Someone HAS to get that room I guess. Shax helps him move rooms…. between two holodecks. Now he hears Shax and T’ana fucking. This is very funny. The first few seasons had a lot of Boimler being the butt of jokes, but those were cause people treated him like shit and didn’t respect him as a human being. This is just accidental and is therefore so much funnier.

Ransom, Mariner, and an Ensign named Gary go to a menagerie to get some Humans the guy in charge owned. But someone lets out THE MOOPSY… a cute little creature that waddles aroung, goes “Moopsy :)” and then SUCKS OUT PEOPLE’S BONES. I fucking love him. He’s perfect. Literally as soon as I saw him I went “that thing is going to kill people”. And I was right. Someone lets it out, and it eats the menagerie owner. Mariner and Ransom solve their differences by talking it out and Mariner confronting her personality flaw of being afraid of failure and causing her own failures intentionally. Wow, imagine that. Also the humans they came to pick up released the Moopsy to kill the owner cause Humans are the worst.

Oh, Rutherford turned down a bunch of premotions before so he just… asks for one and gets it. That’s hilarious. He moves in with Boimler, aaaaand is like “oh, we’re next to the nacelle. Computer, dim windows”. Boom. Solved it. That’s so fucking funny.

This episode was nonstop banger jokes tbh. All the characters are handled amazingly and it even has character growth! AND IT HAS MOOPSY! Moopsy :)

In The Cradle of Vexilon - ENT 7.5/10

Over on Carazonia, a ring world that’s totally not Halo, a benevolent computer named Vexilon has been running the ring world for years, but now it’s starting to get old and is making mistakes, so the captain goes to fix it. Meanwhile, Boimler is down there with T’lyn trying to retrofit some old consoles. But he has to do it very carefully or it’ll explode.

Back on the ship, the others seem to be being hazed by an upper commander and forced to do terrible ensign work.

Boimler is micromanaging his team because he’s afraid of them making mistakes and getting hurt. This is a very relatable and good thing to talk about. The captain does the same thing, and the computer becomes evil, causing severe dangerous terraforming.

Boimler: “Just last week I was their peer. The same level. Now cause of some random promotion I could accidentally send them to die. What gives me the right?”

T’lyn shuts that right now. She gets to the point. She’s a great addition to this series.

They try and prank the officer back but then quickly have to fix the problem cause they feel bad. Alamaraine references. I thought everyone hated that episode but me.

Boimler is killed protecting the others and fixing the problem. But he’s brought back to life. You know how death is. This one was good.

Something Borrowed, Something Green - ENT 9/10

We start with another ship being obliterated, this time Orions. Our first ever onscreen Orion vessel actually.

Umm, hello sexy orion lesbian captain, my name is Liz :)

Tendi gets leave to go visit Orion for her sister’s wedding. She is VERY unhappy about this idea. It’s just boring old traditions. T’lyn and Mariner offer to go with her, which she ALSO hates but decides to let them when they say they want to learn more about Orion cause outsiders rarely get to go.

I fucking LOVE T’Lyn more and more. She’s the best Vulcan since… Spock. She’s a sarcastic little bitch sometimes but like… in that Spock way, where he makes biting funny comments all the time? She clearly does care and wants whats best for people. Unlike most modern Vulcans where they just don’t care about others.

Meanwhile, Boimler and Rutherford have been getting along as roommates, but they’re starting to butt heads being next to each other so much. Can you BELIEVE the other had the AUDACITY to come to the Holodeck dressed as Twain? I WAS GOING AS TWAIN!

Tendi and the girls have to go do some shenanigans because her sister got Bridal Kidnapped, which is apparently just a thing Orions do. I love Tendi. She’s so amazingly perfect at being an Orion but she HATES it, she’s like the opposite of Worf or Quark.

Pheromones are drugs in the Orion society. Alrighty then. Tendi developed a compound that counteracts their effects, and threatens to use it to stop a drug lord, so she immediately folds and gives information.

I don’t need to explain this one.

Tendi has a scene where she breaks down about how she was trained to be an assassin, a “prime”, and thats the “real her”. The others are like “no girl, that’s not the real you. You choose who you wanna be.” Its a very cute scene. It’s interrupted when they find out that Tendi’s sister actually kidnapped herself to drag Tendi here. They have a big fight because “you left and I had to take your place as the prime!” it turns out it’s just cause Tendi’s sister is anxious and feels she’s not good enough to take Tendi’s place. They hug and make up after some mild stabbing.

T’Lyn was here to learn info on the Orions and give that data to the Vulcans. She throws it all out because “getting data from an unwilling subject is unethical.” WOW. A GOOD VULCAN.

This was another great one

Empathological Fallacies - ENT 8.5/10

WE HAVE WATCHED HUNDREDS OF EPISODES OF STAR TREK, AND THIS IS THE FIRST EPISODE THAT DOESN’T HAVE AN IMAGE AT ALL ON MEMORY ALPHA. How is that POSSIBLE? Memory Alpha has a fucking article on GRASS, it’s missing THIS?

Anyways they’re escorting some high level Betazoid women somewhere, and it’s like having three always drunk Lwxana Trois. They’re throwing a big party and flirting with everyone and getting stinking drunk. T’Lyn is unhappy about this. She wants off the ship and back to the Vulcans. But communications are out for some reason. So she DOES go to the party, mostly to inquire when it’ll be over. But everyone is acting… weirder than usual.

Meanwhile, Boimler is invited to the safety’s team’s charades and slam poetry night. He wants it to be a test. But they just want to hang out with him. Thats cute.

T’Lyn is the only one not effected by this. She theorizes that its being caused by the Betazoids. Their cover seems blown so they go nuts and show that they’re betazoid super soldiers.

The Betazoids take over the ship and send it into the Neutral Zone to get back to Betazed. You won’t get away with this! …They get away with it.

Turns out the cause of the emotional outbreaks are… T’LYN! She seems to have some thing that’s causing everyone’s emotions to outbreak. She has a kind of spiral about not being a good enough Vulcan. Mariner talks her down from it and tells her that she’s MORE than good enough, the others who punished her for helping them were being awful. Just cause you’re Vulcan doesn’t mean you can’t be awful. She comes to terms with who she is and this fixes the emotional turmoil.

Boimler’s side story ends when he’s like “why aren’t you all being badass?! Aren’t you safety?” and then they stop the Betazoids with a badass maneuver. Shaxs goes “we were told you were pushing yourself too hard. Safety is about protecting the crew. Phyusically, and mentally. We’re here for you.” I love you, Shax.

Parth Ferengi’s Heart Place - ENT 9/10

THAT FUCKING NAME. HOLY SHIT. More things need to reference Garth Merengi.

Another episode, another ship blowing up. This time it’s the Ferengi.

The Ferengi are visiting! ROM IS HERE! AND LEETA! Holy shit it’s nice to see them. Rom is trying to join the Federation. Um, holy shit. That is uh, that is Huge. Thats the biggest lore thing they could EVER do here.

Meanwhile, the entire Crew is being sent down to Ferenginar to tour the planet and help make a travel brochure. Tendi and Rutherford have to pretend to be married, which is awkward when they realize they actually ARE into each other. Mariner gets up to hanging out and complaining about how everything is good and perfect which weirds her out with her Ferengi friend. Aaaaand boimler plans to review 40 different joints, but then gets addicted to Ferengi television, which is awful corporate shlock. That’s SO funny.

Holy shit. The Paramount logo above his head as he talks about immoral programing. “They put commercials for other shows in the show?! Wow, diabolical.” THE PARAMOUNT LOGO SPARKLES. HOLY SHIT.

Omfg. Rom is playing up being an idiot and Leeta is playing the part of his actually competant wife to fucking scam the Admiral into better deals for Ferenginar. The captain sees through this but he ignores her. That’s so fucking funny.

They make chocolate statues of Tendi and Rutherford. Holy shit, Tendi’s horrifying cone tits. They eventually make a giant show of breaking up just to get out of this mess

The captain fixes the situation by out swindling Rom. Rule of Aquisition #9. Fantastic.

This was mostly an episode of like, small little scenes and character moments. GOD I MISSED CHARACTER MOMENTS.

A Few Badgeys More - ENT 6.5/10

Badgey is back D: He’s taken over a Drookmani salvage ship and it’s going around killing people. He destroys a Bynar this time. Poor Bynars ):

The Cerritos is heading to Bynar space to look into it. Meanwhile, Peanut Hamper is getting out for good behavior, and Tendi is being sent to her hearing. AGIMUS is NOT, but he claims to have knowledge of the Bynar attack and demands for Boimler to come so he can tell him.

We see the two of them claiming they’re going to trick them so they can escape. Clearly not evil.

AGIMUS is very bad at pretending to be good. But I’m so happy to hear Jeffrey Combs

The Cerritos is attacked by Badgey and is almost blown up. Rutherford tries to sacrifice himself so his friends don’t get booped. Mariner goes with him, and Rutherford… makes up with Badgey, hugging him. Badgey has a crisis of hatred, and spits his goodness out as Goodgey. This is some Majin Boo shit. But that didn’t fix the problem, so they stick to another solution and get him in a logic loop. This fixes it for a minute, but then he ejects all his logic. Ooohh we’re gonna get like 50 Badgeys by the end of this.

AGIMUS is doing his thing, but Tendi and Boimler are mostly just letting him so they get any kind of info they can. But it’s pretty obvious he’s got none. But he feels restless cause Peanut Hamper didn’t come like she said. They go and find out she just… wasn’t actually interested in dominating anymore. She’s chilled out. AGIMUS drops the evil stuff too so he can hang out with her more. It’s cute. He’s sent back, but he’s actually interested in rehabilitating.

Badgey brings himself to warp 10 and touches all of space, becoming an omniscient god gaining all knowledge and power from all computers. This makes him realize, wtf is he doing? He has better shit to do. He ascends to another universe. Well, that was sudden. Fair enough, bro.

This one was just alright, but still good.

Caves - ENT 7.5/10

The Beta Shift is back together for a mission! And it’s a Cave Mission! I can’t believe we’ve had so many wordy episode titles tonight and this one is literally just “caves”. They go down to study moss in a cave. Mariner is grumpy cause bad shit always happens in caves and they all look like the same sound set. Aaaand yep, they’re trapped under rubble.

Holy shit it’s a clip show. They talk about all the times they’ve been stuck in caves before and we get small snippets from those times.

The first one is Boimler being stuck with Levi, the conspiracy theorist. I dunno how the fuck this guy is in Starfleet, but tbf, he probably has an AMAZING future as an Admiral. Boimler blows up at him after he goes off on this all being the Vendorians. Anyways it all actually was Vendorians. He’s still a crackpot though.

God I forgot about these guys. They’re from TAS.

The next story is how Rutherford got stuck in a cave with doctor T’ana and had a baby together.

Oh I’m sorry, did you expect T’Ana to be the one who was pregnant? Nope. Mpreg. This truly is a Trek show. The alien guide they’re with dies by a monster but makes a clone baby in Rutherford. They need to survive in the cave while also raising the clone baby. Turns out the monster was just protecting its baby but it sees them being good parents and leads them out of the cave.

The next story is how Mariner is stuck in a cave with the Delta Shifters she hates. Its a cave that makes you old. But they find a section that makes you young and get the stuff they need to contact the ship.

The three of them are angry at each other for not telling each other about their stories. Tendi is stuck in the middle, but then they’re all eaten by the Moss who’s like “YOU ARE NOT ALLOWED TO LEAVE UNTIL I HEAR TENDI’S STORY, I AM CURIOUS”, so Tendi tells the time they were stuck in a turbolift for a few hours and hung out as friends. This pleases the moss. As they wait to be rescued, they keep telling stories to their new friend, the Moss.

Cute one.

The Inner Fight - ENT 7/10

Mariner has a deathwish and is intentionally putting herself in dangherous situations. And at the same time whoever is attacking people in the quadrant is now attacking ex federation officers. So they have to go rescue people like Bev Crusher or Thomas Riker while Mariner is sent with the LD crew to do a boring lazy thing so she doesn’t get herself killed. But then a Klingon bird of prey attacks anyway and they have to beam down to a planet.

While on the planet, they find the people who were seemingly killed by the ship all season! Mariner goes out to fight them and gets her ass kicked by a Klingon.

Meanwhile the captain needs information from a backwater crime planet but everyone blows her off cause she’s Starfleet. I find it more annoying than funny sadly.

Mariner gets pissy and runs off alone. She gets into a fight with the Klingon, who is Ma’ah, remember that guy? He claims his people abandoned him here and betrayed him, so it was his crew up on the bird of prey I guess. They get stuck in a cave cause of a storm (MORE CAVES), and they start talking about this. Why IS Mariner doing all this?

Turns out it’s PTSD :) Yaaay.

Turns out she was friends with someone. Sito. Remember her? She was the Bajoran in TNG who got herself killed following orders. Lower Decks mentioning Lower Decks yay! She’s not cured, but she comes more to terms with it. “there’s been enough fighting and killing”. She ends up getting everyone to team up, but is suddenly transported off planet. They assume she was taken by the Klingons and trick the ship down to the planet and take it, buuuut nope. Where could she be?

Hello there, Not Paris!

Also the captain gets the info she needed because she used people’s hatred of the federation against them, tricking htem into giving information to “a bounty hunter”, one of her officers in disguise. Fair enough. I didn’t like that plot point but I liked the Mariner stuff a lot!

Old Friends, New Planets - ENT 8/10

This looks like a meme.

We flash back to Mariner’s first year in the academy. Gosh, remember the Nova Squadron TNG episode? Who knew that’d be such an important episode for lore. They get everyone back, which is cool.

Back in the present, Nick Locarno is like “I saved you :D You can join me now!” She is…. NOT interested, but pretending to be basically, so she can try and stop him from the inside. Locarno sends out a message to everyone. He’s forming the Nova Fleet, the “first unaligned fleet in the alpha quadrant” (sorry, Maquis). It’s formed of “lower deckers and people who are under appreciated by their stuffy higher ups.” But he also has a Genesis Device that he’ll use as a bomb in case people threaten them. Well, that’s fucked up. At this, Mariner IMMEDIATELY dips, stealing it and running away.

Meanwhile, the Cerritos crew needs to do things against orders so they sneak to Orion to get help. Tendi does BARTER BY COMBAT to force her sister to help them. Buuuut it fails and now her sister owns the Cerritos. To stop this, Tendi offers her the only thing she’d want more. Herself. Tendi noooo ): And it was ALL FOR A SHITTY WARSHIP THAT DOESN’T EVEN WORK. Damn, she’s an asshole ):

Mariner has a talk with Locarno about how he’s a little fucker who’s just mad cause he fucked up and couldn’t take the heat for his failure. He has a breakdown and shows he is in fact still a little stuck up egotistical cadet through all of this.

They break through his shield by THROWING the battleship at it. Boimler gets to do this from the captain’s chair! Yay, that’s badass. Mariner activates the Genesis device, setting it as a bomb, just as Locarno comes and tries to kill her. But she’s rescued by the captain who took the captain’s yacht, first time that thing’s been used. Locarno fucking explodes. Wow, they killed off a canon character. Didn’t know they had it in them.

The Genesis device makes a planet, which they name Locarno. They’re gonna use it for refugees. Neat! Locarno doing something good for the first time.

Everything’s all good! :D No negative reprecussions at all! AND T’Lyn decides to stay, too! She likes it here after all. Oh wait right, Tendi ):

Goodbye Tendi <3 Please please come back in season 5.

Wow. Really good season? It’s so weird to be EXCITED for Star Trek again.

entry.title: X-Men Deep Dive Readalong
entry.content:
I’m reading every X-Men comic. This was a mistake. This will continue to be a mistake. But when have mistakes ever stopped me? Come hang out for some reviews of mid-tier 60s comics!

After I released the first of these btw my boyfriend was like “Babe wtf no, just skip ahead to the late 70s, that’s where everything good is”, but that sounds like a GOOD idea so I’m not gonna do that :)

Strange Tales #120 - May 1964 5.5/10

It seems kinda crazy to think about now, but at one time, the Fantastic Four were THE comic book heroes. The Avengers were B-listers, the X-Men C-listers, and the Fantastic Four were the REAL DEAL. So to try and get some cred and make sure people know the X-Men exist, what better way than a cross over? And it’s a fun idea too, to boot.

Despite that, it’s nothing too special. Ice Man goes on a boat ride to relax, and finds he’s on the same boat as the Human Torch, who is VERY open about his identity. Ice Man discovers he’s on board cause he flirts with his girlfriend, for the record. You’ll figure it out someday, Bobby.

Some pirates try to take the boat, you know, all those pirates who hang out right off the coast of New York City. Torch and Ice Man have to team up to stop them. There’s nothing BAD in this, and the two work together rather well, it just wasn’t really anything special. In the end they defeat the pirates and then Ice Man dips, just walking back across the harbor.

X-Men #6 - July 1964 3/10

If there’s any Marvel character I don’t give a fuck about, it’s Namor. I find him annoying and creepy. His biggest character trait is that he’s horny for Invisible Woman and won’t take no for an answer. I mean, I get being attracted to Sue Storm, but come on dog. So I don’t have massively high hopes for this. Anyways, the plot is that both Xavier and Magneto think Sub-Mariner might be a mutant, and might be a good ally, so it’s a race to find him first.

Okay. Look. Magnetism is a weird force and it’s not very well understood, so I can ignore some of the things Magneto can do that don’t really make any sense…. but there’s no way in FUCK Magneto should be able to create a PSYCHIC ILLUSION OF HIMSELF. I don’t care how big and wrinkly his brain is. Ahhh, we are SERIOUSLY Silver Age right now.

Magneto finds the Submariner first, and he is… screaming and throwing a shit fit, tossing stuff around and breaking things in his castle. Why? Because Sue told him to fuck off again and he’s angry about it. Seriously, it’s his only character trait.

Magneto manages to convince Namor to come and ally with him. The X-Men show up to try and stop this but are easily repelled by Namor. But just as it seems this alliance will hold, Magneto does the one thing Namor cannot abide by.

Magneto makes some sexist remarks and the pussy whipped Sub-Mariner, feminist chad that he is, IMMEDIATELY defects. I still don’t like him, but thank you, Namor.

Namor has known Scarlet Witch for 5 seconds but has to force himself not to fall for her. Bro. Scarlet Witch and Quicksilver have FINALLY had enough of Magneto almost killing them over and over, and dip…. but then Magneto just tells them to come back to him and they do. Y’all, what the hell are you doing? Anyways the X-Men just got their asses kicked over and over, but Magneto being a sexist caused him to lose, the end.

Fantastic Four #28 - July 1964 4/10

Another crossover, this time over on the FF’s full comic. So there’s two villains, the Thinker and the Puppet Master, who are trying to destroy the Fantastic Four. The Puppet Master mind controls Professor X and makes him command the X-Men to destroy the Fantastic Four. They’re all very upset at the idea of doing this, but hey, the boss man said.

The X-Men basically dogwalk the Fantastic Four because they don’t actually want to fight and are more like “what the FUCK is going on”. After being easily defeated, for SOME reason the Puppet Master and Thinker show themselves and go “Yeah so we own you now”. The X-Men are like “the fuck you do?” and even though Professor X brain controls them, they break it just enough to destroy the thing Puppet Master is using to control him. The two are then very easily defeated and escape in a rocket.

It ends with the X-Men leaving and Reed going “gosh gee those X-Men are great, everyone should buy their comics”.

The most interesting part of this is the lore drop that Alicia Masters, The Thing’s girlfriend, is Mastermind’s step daughter. Which is kinda interesting. More crossovers in the future possibly?

X-Men #7 - September 1964 5/10

Oh hey, the Scarlet Witch is no longer green! She’s kinda more… purple than scarlet, but thats fine.

The X-Men have graduated and Scott is now their leader. But Xavier IS still here, and he introduces Scott to a project he’s been working on, a machine called Cerebro that can scan for Mutants so they can find more people to join their group.

Also interestingly, Ice Man now has a face. He was just kinda lumpy before. He looks a lot better like this, but looks a little Silver Surfery.

Everyone is so flirty with Jean, but she seems to only have eyes for one of them. The only one who doesn’t care (or doesn’t PRETEND to care so he’s not outed as gay). First mention of this plot point!

Meanwhile, Magneto is also hunting for mutants, and finds The Blob! He then… probes his mind??? Which like, again, not really a thing, but okay. After they fight a little bit, Blob remembers his spat with the X-Men and agrees to join Magneto cause he’s pissed about what they did to him.

There’s a big fight where the X-Men are, as usually, kinda trounced. But they win because Magneto decides “oh I can just kill them now, who cares if the Blob is also there” and throws a fucking missile at them. It ONLY hits the Blob, who goes “WOW. Fuck this shit I’m out.” and leaves. The rest of Magneto’s brotherhood are like “Why the FUCK did you do that?” and also abandons him over it so they all flee. Magneto once again clutching defeat from the jaws of victory.

This one was whatever, but it was the first with NO training segment at all.

X-Men #8 - November 1964 5.5/10

Never heard of this guy before. I wonder if I’m gonna find someone who only ever showed up once.

NONE of these people have ANY chill about Jean, I swear. Also everyone has death defying training to do, dodging shit and stuff, and Jean’s training is uh…. doing cross stitching with her mind. Cause she girl.

I want to vomit.

Beast almost causes a fucking race riot because he rescued a kid from almost dying and they invented a guy about it. Glad not much has changed since the 60s, huh? Now I wanna cry. Anyways Beast is fed up, which does make sense, but he’s like “HUMANS CANNOT BE TRUSTED, ALL I CARE ABOUT NOW IS MYSELF” which feels… VERY un-Hank McCoy to me, but I guess I only really know about the more modern Beast. I feel this’d be more like… Angel’s thing. He was also in that riot!

Also Cyclops calls Xavier, who’s like “Yeah I’m busy diving into caves in the middle of Europe, chat with you later hun bun”. What the fuck is he doing??

Beast goes to become a wrestler and gets beaten by some guy, Unus, who’s clearly a mutant with some power to make it so you can’t get near him. Beast sees him also be buddy buddy with the Mastermind, which worries him, even though he clearly doesn’t care about the X-Men anymore.

Unus wants to join the Brotherhood, but is told he has to defeat the X-Men first, which seems like a bit of a tall order from a group who can’t do it themselves. He helps rob a bank to get their attention, and then dog walks the X-Men, as usual. Honestly, this guy mostly feels like a retread of The Blob but with arrogance instead of stupidity as his character trait.

At least they defeat him in a pretty interesting way. The Beast comes back to develop a beam that enhances Unus’ power. Which I guess is just easy to do, that seems useful. They assume he’s already working for Magneto and try to stop him, but it’s too late, he makes Unus super powerful… but not he can’t even touch anything. Welp. Good job, Beast, you killed him. He’s going to starve in a few days. Or die of oxygen deprevation.

That is actually straight up what happens, they let him run around for a while and starve him out. Then Beast is like “I can cure you, but if you ever cross us again, we’ll just shoto you again and then break the machine so fuck off.” and so he fucks off.

The Beast decides to rejoin, just…. for some reason. He decides that’s where he belongs. All that stuff about “HUMANS AREN’T WORTH THE DIRT ON MY SHOE” stuff is just water under the bridge I guess.

X-Men #9 - January 1964 3/10

Oh boy, another crossover event! Real excited to see more contrived reasons for super heroes to fight! Who’s the other team today? The Avengers? Pff, get away from THOSE losers, they’ll never take off. And what’s that? A new villain introduced?

Oh… Lucifer. Huh.

Yeah no, I don’t think you can use that name.

Any time I see panels like this it just reminds me of when Homestar Runner would make fun of old timey comics

Anyways, The X-Men are getting messages from Xavier, who is somehow fighting Lucifer by himself in some cave, whoever the fuck that is. They head off to join him in the Balkans. Meanwhile, the Avengers are just… wandering around kinda harassing people? The team right now appears to be Thor, Iron Man, Cap, and Antman. And I THINK that’s Wasp? She’s not even on the cover, but DOES flit around and do things, but she has a pretty miniscule presence.

They can’t kill Lucifer, which apparently Xavier was totally planning to do, since he put a dead man’s switch to a nuke. Just that easy. Lucifer is just a… guy. Who wants to rule the world. He’s like Wish.com Dr. Doom. The Avengers are searching for Lucifer, and Xavier tells the X-Men to stall them so they don’t kill Lucifer, because again, the Avengers are WELL KNOWN for murdering every villain they come across. This is course gives us a chance to have these nerds fight. Also you’d EXPECT them to mention that Angel and Stark met before but uh, they don’t. This also ends very quickly cause Xavier just… knocks Lucifer out with his brain and then tells Thor “quit it” and Thor quits it.

Silly Charles, we will all return to Lucifer one day.

They just let him go after he gets all sad that they ruined his nuke, and Xavier makes some comment about how he was the cause for his legs not working, but everyone is like “well I guess we’ll find out eventually.”

This was kinda dumb. Uninteresting villain, and the Avengers match up was like… nothing, then they just walk off. They’re not even there at the ending.

X-Men #10 - March 1965 5/10

There’s some news about an Antarctic expedition finding a a wild tarzan-ass guy in Antartica with a saber tooth tiger. They even compare him to Tarzan. They assume he’s a mutant, but Xavier confirms he’s not. But he says they can go see him to cure their boredom cause there’s been no violence recently. Well I’m glad we’re doing this just for the fuck of it. Honestly I wish we’d get MORE comics of them just being bored and hanging out tbh. Not everything has to be a world ending event.

While exploring Antarctica they find a tunnel that leads to The Savage Land, where dinosaurs still live. Some… kinda ugly ones but look, it was a LONG time before Jurassic Park made Dinosaurs better forever. Though there’s an Archeoptrix, which is feathered, and thats cute :)

While exploring, Jean is knocked out and kidnapped by some guys, and they’re driven off by Ka-zar and his tiger Zabu. They are not enemies whatsoever, and are in fact, on the same side, but because everyone is allergic to TALKING they start beating the shit out of each other.

Luckily Ka-zar has REALLY bad ADHD and is distracted by some guy he hates. He beats the shit out of them, then afterwards when the X-Men say “hey let’s be friends” he goes “oh, okay.” I guess he forgot.

Angel is captured too and he and Jean need to survive a poorly drawn T-Rex. Jean is too terrified to be of any help because She’s Girl, ignore the fact that she’d be PERFECT for getting out of this cause she doesn’t care if she’s tied up in ropes. Ka-zar and the others show up and cause a mammoth stampede.

Th-then don’t? Comics are a visual medium???

They rescue Jean and Angel and try being like “Ah, we’ve made a true friend, Ka-zar, thanks for fighting with-“ but Ka-zar goes “Fuck off, leave.” so they fuck off and leave, and then the mammoth fill the tunnel with rocks.

I mean… it’s fine I guess? Not as exciting as the first time in the Savage Lands should be, I feel.
entry.summary: I’m reading every X-Men comic. This was a mistake. This will continue to be a mistake. But when have mistakes ever stopped me? Come hang out for some reviews of mid-tier 60s comics!

entry.title: LizstarTrek - Discovery Season 3 episodes 11 - 13
entry.content:
Every Sunday my Twitch subs and I watch Star Trek in my Discord. Here are my reviews and thoughts on each of the episodes as I see it. If you’re curious about a nerd’s views on Star Trek episodes, please read on, I go quite in depth with some of these episodes! I’ve watched some Star Trek before but not all of it!

I know literally nothing about Discovery, except for The Burn, and that it leads into Strange New Worlds. So uh… I’ve been dreading this one. But hey, who knows! Maybe it’ll surprise me!!

It has not so far.

Su’Kal - DIS 1.5/10

Our episode starts with Adira reconnecting with their Mind Boyfriend, who apologizes for avoiding them, they’ve just felt weird being stuck in Adira’s head. Stamets is like “ohhh you’re lucky we’re at a memorial service right now or I would be giving you a piece of my MIND.” I love Gay Dad Stamets.

They reach where the crashed ship they got the distress signal from was. There’s still a lifesign on board, Kelpien. That was YEARS ago, but the person in the distress signal was gregnant, so that explains it. Book risks his life to go into the radiation nebula to get a scan, and they also find out that there’s a planet made out of pure dilithium, and Michael theorizes this is the source of the burn. No one, in all the 100 years, go this distress signal at the source of the burn and then found this? Yes, there’s radiation, but there were ways about that in the 2300s.

BOOK TOOK THE CAT INTO THE RADIATION ZONE?! JUST TAKE HER OFF THE SHIP BEFORE DOING DANGEROUS STUFF, BOOK.

They send a message to the admiral- wait, subspace beacons are down. They literally said they couldn’t send messages very far. They made it a plot point. How are they- whatever. The Admiral wishes them luck and also tells them that the Orions are attacking. Gee, maybe we should have killed her when we had the chance?! Anyways, they send down Michael, Saru, and Culber to the planet, with Tilly in charge on the ship. But don’t worry, Tilly gets advice from Michael before she’s put in charge :) Look, usually it’d be “oh she’s getting advice from her best friend with experience”, but BECAUSE MICHAEL HAS TO DO EVERYTHING, it’s VERY annoying.

They land on the planet and are weirdly teleported in in phases, and they’re all no longer the same species they were supposed to be. Michael is Trill, Culber is Bajoran, and Saru is a Human!! Saru’s actor is…. one of those people who just already seems weirdly inhuman already? Like kinda Odo’s character, you look at him and go “yeah, he’d play an alien in Star Trek.” Anyways they appear to be in a holo program. They find the Kelpien they’re here to rescue, but he’s mentally just a child, all he knows is this program, and he gets scared of them and runs away. There’s also apparently a “monster” in this program? Gotta say, Saru and Culber are VERY much the correct people for this, trying to handle first contact with a man child. ….why is Michael here? Yes, cause she’s the main character I guess. I know.

Back on the ship, a Federation ship makes it way to them. They send the correct response calls, but don’t respond to hails. Uh, shields up? No? Okay, Tilly.

Michael finds the Monster, which is a Dark Templar lookin’ mother fucker. It chases her around. Neat. I feel like if this were more popular I’d see a LOT of porn of this thing. Anyways she runs away and finds the Kelpien, and pretends to be a hologram teaching about social interraction. The Kelpien is weirding us out in the chat, because like, he’s SUPPOSED to be an adult child, but the acting is like an unflattering autistic representation.

The “federation ship” is actually Ossyra, the pirate, of course. So they activate their cloaking devi- THEIR WHAT?! THEIR FUCKING WHAT?!?! You can’t just fucking drop that on me, that’s a VERY important thing. They finally establish communications, and Ossyra tries to break Tilly down and she’s like “nope :)” Book goes down on his ship to rescue them while they fight the pirate.

Meanwhile, the kid has an emotional outburst and seems to create another Burn wave, but it’s stopped after Saru starts signing a lullaby to him. Well at least Saru solved this one. Culber comes up with what happened to him, somehow, just by seeing this. At some point in utero he became connected with the Dilithium. And when he gets really sad, that causes dilithium to explode.

….The pirates beam in and take Discovery. Um. Their shields are up?? They use a mind jacking machine and force Stamets to do their thing, just as Michael returns with Book to see them leave. Welp. Adira went down to the planet with meds to try and keep them alive, but that’s not gonna matter. Everyone’s dead, the end. Apparently the spore drive can also just take Ossyra’s ship with them. Also, why the fuck didn’t EVERYONE beam up with Michael? Why even leave them down there? So Saru can do even less???

They basically made this episode so that Ossyra could win. They broke every law in the show to make it so that Tilly would lose, so Michael can save the day next episode. THat is VERY annoying :) Tilly’s first time in the captain’s chair and she loses it due to cheating and bad writing.

There Is a Tide… - DIS 3/10

Remember Zareh, the guy they exiled out to the ice to die who was just harassing random miners? He’s here working with the pirates now, he’s still a shithead. He and everyone else is insulting Tilly and saying she did a shitty job because they just easily took the ship. Yes, please, KEEP making it clear Tilly did a bad job that WAS NOT HER FAULT, IT’S JUST CAUSE THE WRITERS WANTED HER TO LOSE.

Ossyra is trying to do a false flag attack on the Federation HQ, basically, but is interrupted when Michael and Book show up. ……..What? They black alerted here. “Oh they used a transwarp”…. THAT LEADS RIGHT TO OUTSIDE THE FEDERATION HQ? How fucking convenient!!!! Anyways they crash into the cargo bay to get back on Discovery. Hmm. Okay.

Don’t worry. She will.

This image is basically Discovery in a nutshell.

I love how Ossyra has to KEEP being “take them alive, kill no one”. Can’t kill any important characters.

Michael gets stabbed in the leg, cauterizes the wound with a phaser, and sends a last mesasge to her mom on Vulcan like “I might not see you again, goodbye”. Yeah, you can send a fucking message from the middle of space to Vulcan through a ship with shields up, through a fucking shielded and cloaked Federation HQ. Sure.

The bridge crew knocks out their guards and gets to work retaking the ship, which is badass, Tilly leading them. Are you all going to give her this OTHER chance and then fucking yank it away from her and have Michael save the day?

Ossyra makes a preposal to the Admiral. Let’s COMBINE the Federation and the Emerald Chain, with us working together, we can help everyone! A NEW federation! :D With blackjack! And slavery!

Stamets is unslaved so this guy can talk to him. His name is Aurelio, and he’s actually a kind of nice friendly guy, he wants to know more about the sporedrive so he can replicate it. He seems to GENUINELY think they’re all doing good things for the world. Ossyra has basically kept him in the dark. Stamets tries to convince him to stop this and help them save his kid and partner. He very, VERY directly calls Adira his kid. GAY DAD STAMETS.

Yet another person got spaced. Do they have a quota? Some kind of kink?

The reason Aurelio trusts Ossyra is because she bought him some medicine that solved a defect when he was a kid, and now he’s still around and is a scientist helping out! He even developed the pesticide that they used to extort that planet a few episodes ago. When Stamets is like “uh, they were using that to extort them so they could extinct a species?” Aurelio is like “um, what?” but THAT scene is fucking ended with Michael knocking him out. Stamets is like “oh thank god now we can go back and save Hugh and the others.” Michaels like “No, I’m here to kidnap you so they can’t use the spore drive :)” Stamets has a fucking breakdown, and a really good line of “MY WHOLE LIFE IS STUCK IN THAT NEBULA!” and Michael fucking vulcan neck pinches him. Fuck you, Michael.

The peace talks fall through cause the Admiral is like “yeah sure, all of this SOUNDS good but you’re STILL a slaver murderer with endless crimes under her belt, so we’ll totally be down if you also stand trial.” and she of course storms out. She also immediately starts showing herself as a shithead and Aurelio is like “oh maybe she IS evil.”

Ryn, the Andorian, is like “I’M NOT AFRAID OF YOU. I’VE SEEN REAL BRAVERY.” He is talking about Michael. He’s also killed.

Oh good, we get to see Stamets yell at Michael AGAIN. I mean, the first scene was pretty powerful and makes me hate her even more, why not just DO IT AGAIN? THis time she spaces him in a bubble so that Starfleet can rescue him.

The episode ends with them meeting the Spore Data AI which has hid itself in these drones. Oh my GOD they wanted to make Star Wars so bad.

That Hope Is You Part 2 - DIS 1/10

Hey, HERE’S the part 2.

Back on the planet, we see Adira landing and giving them the medicine. They ALSO have their Mind Boyfriend with them, which the… holodeck somehow recognizes and makes a physical form for so everyone can see them. Um. This is 125 year old technology, if IT can see them why the FUCK couldn’t any of the medical people? So that it’d be exciting in the final episode? Yes. So it could be exciting in the final episode.

They drag Stamets away kicking and screaming going “Michael was right :)” Fuck everything.

LOL Ni’Var is here cause Michael sent a last message to them, somehow. They’re here to save the day and rejoin the Federation. But now Michael is like “No, let us go, so that more people don’t die. You can trust me. Please :)” Um, you were demoted for insubordination, we demonstrably can not. But she IS the Special Boy.

Ossyra tortures Book to try and get info about where the Dilithium planet is. Aurelio is like “wait, torture? But that’s mean >:(“ so she chokes him out to get him to shut up. I think he might be the bad guy!!

Meanwhile, Saru is trying to talk to Su’Kal, the Kelpien kid, to gently get info and convince him they’re here to help, without starting another Burn. I still am uncomfortable watching this kid.

The bridge crew is being oxygen starved. Everyone is passing out, except Owo, who is really good at holding her breath. So she’s not dying while everyone else is. So she raises her death flags, says “I love you all” and goes off to try and save the day by herself.

Hey, y’all remember how I hate how the turbo lifts are just like a giant empty space with a bunch of boxes flying around randomly? Like Willy Wonka’s glass elevators? It’s very JJ Trek movie coded? You know how I HATE those? The big action climax is Book and Michael fighting through this, after having escaped from Ossyra.

Why do we have a data wall that eats people? Why does Ossyra then shove her into that data wall while having her helpless instead of actively killing her? Michael shoots through the data wall and kills Ossyra, then escapes it. Um. Okay. She takes the ship back and restores life support. Owo is alive! The AI sphere data sacrificed hitself to save her. Well, surprised. Kinda dumb, but surprised. Everyone gets back to the bridge and Tilly’s like “oh, I’m done being the XO. It’s back to you, Michael, please lead us, you’re the only one that can do it.” I AM GOING TO MELT DOWN INTO A PILE OF ANGRY GOO.

Also apparently Book can do Spore transport cause of his empathy magic. They drop the warp core to blast a way out and black alert back to the planet.

They convince Su’Kal to turn off the holograms, and then he has to for some reason see the data entry of what happend 125 years ago. To do… something. He HAS to. Yes, him seeing his mom die caused the burn. Which like, that was OBVIOUS? We didn’t need to see it for no reason.

Discovery shows up, saves the day. And then we get a slam poetry session with Michael as we see everything being fixed. They make Gray a robot body. Stamets is VERY pissed at Michael, understandable. Also Saru is going back to Kaminar and being written off the show. That was…. just thrown in there in a one off line. What in the fuck?????

The Admiral gets her here and goes “Just a while ago I was standing here and yelling at you for not doing things the right way.” NO. WHAT SHE DID WAS WRONG. SHE SHOULD NOT HAVE DONE IT. They give her captaincy of Discovery, because of COURSE they do. I think I called this in the first few episodes, “this will end with Michael becoming captain”. I just didn’t think it’d be done in this stupid of a way.

Let’s undercut Tilly even more by the way. Michael is now captain and goes off to save the world again and again and again and

I hated this. Every fucking writing decision in this was so bad and dumb. Honestly, most of this season. The only thing in this season I really actually liked was the Stamets, Culber, and Adira stuff. And they had their agency ripped away from them in these last few episodes. So that Michael could be the one to save everyone.

Neli actually made a VERY good comparison about this and why I fucking hate Michael. It’s like what people say is wrong with Wesley Crusher. He was designed as a central point character, and solved the problem in a few episodes, and people make fun about that. But then that… stopped.

Michael is like if they NEVER stopped doing that with Wesley Crusher. She is…. bad. She is bad. She is a bad character. And it sucks, cause as a CHARACTER she’s fine, but she’s written SO POORLY.

God. I hated this. It’s better than Picard season 1, I guess. That’s not saying much…

entry.title: X-Men Deep Dive Readalong
entry.content:
I never really got into comics. I mean, I got into MANGA, especially yuri, but not really comics, y’know? And yet, despite that, I’ve always been a fan of the X-Men. I wore out my X-Men VHS tapes as a kid, and strangely, the story of a disenfranchized group of people resonated with me, and still does to this day! But despite that, I’ve never really gotten into comics.

Comics are EXTREMELY varied, I know that much. It all depends on the writers and artists that day, really. There are highs, and there are lows. And I dunno if I’m gonna finish this, or even get far, but I’mma do my best to read all the X-Men comics I can. Cause why the hell not? Seems like a good place to start if I wanna get into comics.

But if I wanna get started, where do I ACTUALLY start? And what order do I read the comics in? If I wanted to read every single possible X-Men comic, it would be… a lot. A loooot. Do I read the standalone comics about just one character? Like, do I read all eight billion standalone Wolverine comics that have NOTHING to do with the rest of the X-Men? Luckily for me, there are a lot of lists out there by nerds who’ve done the reading and are making suggestions. Unlucky for me, most of them do not agree with each other.

For the sake of making things easier for me, I’m just following the list here: https://ultimatexmenreadingorder.com/ This has the rule that for it to count, it’s about the team. So at least three members of the team have to show up. This does mean I’ll have to read SOME of the solo series but not every single issue of Deadpool cause he was on the team for like 5 days or whatever. Though apparently there are a few issues in this list that don’t actually involve the X-Men but are important on a lore basis for understanding what the fuck is going on, so I guess I appreciate that one.

This project is daunting, but very interesting for me. I do really like the X-Men, but my experience has been through cultural osmosis and through watching the movies, mostly. And a few episodes of the show as a kid over and over on VHS, which is why Jubilee is my favorite member of the X-Men :3. But this is why the other day I was talking to my boyfriend about the X-Men and I went “who the fuck is Mr. Sinister that name is very dumb”.

I am doing my studying, and by the end of this, I am sure I will be a MASTER of X-Menology. Or I will crash and burn. Only time will tell. But let’s get started!

The X-Men #1 - September 1963 4/10

The introduction to the X-Men is an extremely simple silver-age comic. To be fair, it has to introduce all of the X-Men, and uh, it TRIES to do that, I guess. It introduces us first to Charles Xavier, or Professor X, the leader of the group. He runs a school for gifted kids who are actually Mutants, which in this are basically just people with super powers. He has mind reading and can speak over long distances into people’s minds, which he usually just uses to yell at his students to get to class already, which is kinda funny.

This comic introduces the five members of the team, which are:

1) Hank McCoy, the Beast. One of my all time favorite X-Men, he’s practically unrecognizable here. He’s a big goofball brute who forces kisses on women and is kinda The Big Dumb Guy of the group. He’s also, notably, just Human looking but with big hairy hands and feet. I immediately do not like him here, I can’t wait for him to get better.

2) Bobby Drake, Ice Man. He’s the wise cracking teen of the group with something to prove. He’s notable cause while all the other members of the team wear super suits or whatever, he’s just a walking snowman in boots. ALSO while every other member here is flirting with Jean Gray, he notably doesn’t care and constantly makes fun of them about it. I’m sure that won’t mean anything down the line.

3) Slim Summers, Cyclops. Yes, Slim. He’s kind of serious, no-nonsense. Not a lot of personality here, generic heroics. Honestly, he’s pretty accurate to how I picture Cyclops now.

4) Warren Worthington, The Angel. He’s also kind of serious and no-nonsense, but a bit more cocky. Honestly I also found him kind of boring, but I’ve never really cared about Angel much.

5) Jean Grey, Marvel Girl. God, I forgot they called her Marvel Girl. She seems like a nice proper girl but has a bit of a girlboss streak, y’know, for 1963. When Beast plants an unwanted kiss on her cheek she fucking swings him around in the air like a ragdoll. Go Jean. She’s the newest member of the team, joining in the middle after an invitation from Xavier.

The comic is as follows: Every member is introduced, doing some exercises for their eventual goal of protecting mankind, then we’re introduced to the villain, Magneto. Xavier believes some mutants will use their powers for evil so he’s training mutants to help stop them, and sure enough, “the first of the evil mutants shows themselves”. His plan is… confusing. He goes to a random military base and fucks with their missile launches for like, a week. I guess they’re just randomly launching missiles out of this New York military base, was that normal in the 60s??? After he gets bored of that, he walzes in and goes “This is my base now, I will use it to start the revolution where I rule the world”. He also declares himself Homo Superior, which means that whole thing started instantly, which is neat.

The X-Men hear of this and go to save the day. After a few pages of fighting, of which basically only Cyclops can do anything to him and Jean does literally nothing (this might become a theme), Magneto gets away. The general there congratulates them and they fly back home on what appears to be a commercial airline.

For an introduction, it’s…. fine. There’s some typos which is wild, the art is whatever, and the characters are annoying to boring, but like, I dunno. Could get good eventually.

The X-Men #2 - November 1963 6/10

In this issue we’re introduced to the strongest villain the X-Men have ever had to face… THE VANISHER! He uh, he vanishes. He can teleport, that’s his power. He uses this to rob a bank and then disappear with the money before they can arrest him. He also uses this to grab some defense plans and threatens to sell them to the commies. He looks absolutely ridiculous.

This comic is, once again, half them dealing with the villain, half them training. This time they have the Danger Room, though. Over all I liked this a bit more. The banter was a little more on point, very silver age but fun enough, and while the villain is very goofy…. he’s very goofy. And I like that.

He defeats them easily by just… leaving with the thing he was stealing. And then when he shows up again he’s easily beaten by Xavier, who uses his mind powers to make him forget who he is, and that he even has powers. Wow, that’s fucked up!

This issue also introduces three important things and reinforces one last one. One, after the last issue, the X-Men have become super famous, and have groupies. There’s some people who don’t trust them cause they’re hiding their identities, but there’s no real angst about Mutants yet. Two, Angel is SUPER popular with the ladies. Three, he and Jean seem to have a thing going on. And finally Four, the X-Men LOVE to fight with each other, and don’t seem to like each other very much.

Tales of Suspense #49 - January 1964 N/A

I have ALREADY run into a problem with this X-Men chronology I’m following. This recommends I read this, Tales of Suspense #49. That’s Iron Man’s comic, and is the first time an X-Man meets another super hero. In this case it’s Angel. I uh, I could not find this issue for uh, rent. And I’m not buying it for 400 fucking dollars online. So I just read a plot summary.

Very stupid, from what it sounds like. The Angel is flying back to the mansion right over a Stark weapons facility right as Stark is testing some nuclear explosions. Stark tries to warn him but the explosion turns Angel evil for some reason, and then Stark has to try and stop him from joining the evil mutants. This ends with him deciding he needs to prove there’s still good in Angel by nearly killing himself and causing the Angel to snap out of it and save him. Xavier promises to help Iron Man down the way for helping an X-men, the end.

Probably important lore wise and historically (AND its my first “two heroes must fight for dumb reasons” crossover!) but uh, doesn’t sound like a very exciting story! Honestly I hear that Iron Man kinda sucked back then.

The X-Men #3 - January 1964 5/10

The theme of this comic is exaggeration. While in the first few books, no one really had much of a character beyond arguing with each other and fawning over Jean, here it’s expanded ever so slightly. We will slowly take these characters and stretch their character so that they’re something more unique and recognizable, I’m sure.

Unfortunately, this issue DOES still hyper focus on everyone being into Jean. Including Professor X, which creeps me the fuck out. Even Iceman can’t resist her wiles. I know this wasn’t exactly written for women in mind, but I can’t help but read this and go “eurgh”.

The two winners here for characterization are Cyclops and Beast. Cyclops was always kind of a stick in the mud, but they REALLY cement it here. He’s downright surly, and he’s the first character to be like “yo maybe having these mutant powers blows”. The closest we got before was Angel going “I have to wear a binder to hide my wings and that hurts”. Oh also important, Cyclops has a new name! He was called Slim Summer for the first two issues, but here he’s called Scott. Much better.

Then we have the Beast. Before this issue, the Beast was kind of the bumbling strong dumb guy. He hits on women, he’s goofy. He’s still got a bit of that, but they cement something else about him: he’s a book lover and considers himself a sophisticant.

See? Now THIS is character.

The plot as it were is that the X-Men are looking for new Mutants and Xavier senses one. They find him at the local carnival, a man named The Blob. His mutant power is he cannot be moved or hurt in any way. They invite him back to their mansion to test him to see if he wants to join the X-Men. He’s kind of an asshole, but frankly they’re all rude to him too, ESPECIALLY Scott. Lots of calling him fat. Ha ha, did you know he’s fat?

Anyways The Blob has no actual reason to join them, and is like “nah, I’m way better than all of you, I’ll just rule now that I know I’m superior to humans”, and takes over the carnival. He sends his men to the mansion to ransack it and take all of the X-Men’s technology that they appear to have?

The X-Men get trounced before Jean saves the day by psychically taking off her blindfold and cutting her restraints. But uh, she had to be TOLD to do that by Xavier. Alright. Xavier also uses some technology to enhance his mind powers and erase everyone’s memories, the end.

There was enough in this comic that annoyed me that I can’t really call it GOOD, but I’m seeing something form here.

The X-Men #4 - February 1964 6.5/10

The one thing every single one of these comics has in common is that the X-Men are ALWAYS training in the danger room. We need to show them doing an obstacle course in every single issue. I’m already starting to gloss over it.

But this issue thankfully focuses mostly on the actual plot, and reintroduces Magneto. I haven’t mentioned it, but Magneto is one of my favorite villains of all time. I love a guy where I know why they’re doing what they’re doing and can understand and feel for them but still know I gotta stop em. Magneto is like that. Well, usually. Here he’s just kind of an asshole who believes he’s superior to everyone and thus must rule. We’ll get to the WW2 stuff eventually I guess.

We’re introduced to his group of lackies, and it’s KIND of funny how I can barely tell the difference between the groups. They’re both a guy at the top who they all show allegiance to, but when he’s not bossing them around they just fight each other and are petty as fuck.

We’ve got four lackies.

Toad: His power set isn’t even really explained, he’s just a gross guy with a psychophantic personality. The Mastermind: He can produce illusions. He’s actually the one here I know the least. He’s kind of a self absorbed asshole. Scarlet Witch: Girl. Magneto saved her as a kid so she feels allegience. She’s shown to not want to do unneccesary harm, which is neat, anti-villains already. It’s weird that she’s green on the cover, she’s red in the comic. Quicksilver: Scarlet Witch’s brother, who’s only here because Scarlet Witch is. He is the least evil, and in the end secretly foils Magneto’s plans so that he doesn’t blow up an entire country of people.

It’s neat to have a cast of villains to counter as the foil to our heroes. Magneto’s plan is to take over a small South American nation, which he does easily using Mastermind’s powers creating a fake illusion army. The X-Men come in and try to stop him. The MVP here is probably Cyclops, with the Beast taking the idiot ball.

In the end, the Brotherhood of Evil Mutants flees, but Xavier is injured by an explosive trap that Beast almost sets off after not listening to stop. Basiclly, Xavier, the paraplegic, has to dive out of his wheelchair in front of Beast to block an explosion. I feel there were better ways to accomplish this. This ends up knocking out Xavier’s powers, which sets up something for the next issue, which is kinda neat I guess.

Reading this comic and seeing this page in particular actually made me realize something. I said I had never read any comics like this before. That’s not actually true… There was one “super hero” comic I read religiously as a kid. And that’s the Sonic Archie comics, which were VERY inspired by this. God, I remember so many of those fucking comics where they did this EXACT thing, showing a guy and then some floating heads above him talking about him. I wouldn’t be surprised if Ken Penders was DIRECTLY inspired by this while making his dumbass Knuckles comics. I know he was a big comic head, at least.

The X-Men #4 - May 1964 5/10

I love how every Stan Lee comic starts like this.

YOU LOVED THE LAST ISSUE. YOU HAVE NO CHOICE.

Xavier is now useless, so the X-men are kind of despondant without him. Jean’s parents come to visit which doesn’t really go anywhere, they just think its a normal school, but it’s an opportunity to accidentally lock Cyclops in the Danger Room so he has to do some actiony scenes. Every SINGLE issue something like this happens. Them pretending to be normal also means we see everyone’s outlook on being Mutants again. Cyclops is still all sad about being able to accidentally kill people, and the Beast says he’d much rather just be a normal honors student. The others are happy enough with their arrangements.

The Brotherhood is back already and is actively hunting for the X-Men. They’re hiding out on an asteroid orbiting Earth, which is wild.

I haven’t mentioned it yet, but every single picture of Magneto in these comics has him look like this. He’s gormless as hell. Bro has no gorm.

Anyways, plot happens. They see a trackmeet on TV and watch a guy who’s a mutant rile up a mob by being better than everyone else. I bet he’d be beloved if his name was Michael Phelps. This is the first time the comics REALLY dwell upon the idea that Humans hate Mutants. Magneto has been drilling it into everyone’s heads, but they have friends in Washington and adoring mobs of fangirls in issue 2, so this is the firest time it’s really a THING.

Anyways, turns out it’s actually Toad leading them into a trap. The Brotherhood kidnaps Angel (after saying they’ve never defeated Magneto without Xavier’s help, despite that basically being the case in the first issue), and try to get him to tell them where the mansion is.

Scarlet Witch’s job is to be a snivelling weak girl who doesn’t WANT to be evil but can’t say no to the big bad guy. She eventually DOES break some controls so that Magneto can’t throw the X-Men out an airlock once they show up, but nothing really comes of that. He tries to kill her, Quicksilver stands up to him and fights back, but then just goes along with Magneto when he escapes, cause I guess Magneto has a short attention span.

The X-Men save the day after Cyclops almost burns up in the atmosphere, and Magneto limps off for who knows where. And it turns out Xavier was just PRETENDING to have lost his powers! He was TESTING them! Wow! What an asshole!

This one was fine, mostly kind of boring and samey. Bit of a rehash already.

Anyways, that’s five comics so far, kind of, so I’mma take a break for today.
entry.summary: I never really got into comics. I mean, I got into MANGA, especially yuri, but not really comics, y’know? And yet, despite that, I’ve always been a fan of the X-Men. I wore out my X-Men VHS tapes as a kid, and strangely, the story of a disenfranchized group of people resonated with me, and still does to this day! But despite that, I’ve never really gotten into comics.

entry.title: LizstarTrek - Discovery Season 3 episodes 6 - 10
entry.content:
Every Sunday my Twitch subs and I watch Star Trek in my Discord. Here are my reviews and thoughts on each of the episodes as I see it. If you’re curious about a nerd’s views on Star Trek episodes, please read on, I go quite in depth with some of these episodes! I’ve watched some Star Trek before but not all of it!

I know literally nothing about Discovery, except for The Burn, and that it leads into Strange New Worlds. So uh… I’ve been dreading this one. But hey, who knows! Maybe it’ll surprise me!!

It has not so far.

Scavengers - DIS 3.5/10

Discovery has been retrofitted with futuristic tech. A whole lot of “programmable matter” and holograms comiong out of the new ugly combadges which like, I dunno why you’d need any of this. “Oh now it connects to your biodata so only you can use that station”. That seems like a HORRIBLE idea, people die on this ship like flies.

Anyways Book sends Michael a message like “yo, I found a black box like you said you’ve been looking for”. Based on black box data, it seems the burn didn’t happen at once, but was instead a wave, and if we get enough black box data showing time and location at explosion, we can possibly triangulate the origin point. Yeah that seems important, sure. Also Book might be missing. But Michael’s like “okay, let’s go get it right now :)” and Captain Saru is like “uh no, we’ve been ordered to wait here because they’ll need our help at any point in the next 12 hours.” “Oh, it won’t take me that long :)” “Um. Michael, I said no.”

I hate this plot point. Michael being really into insubordination, after spending two seasons learning that was A Bad Thing, especially with how much she CLAIMS to respect Saru and his authority, she sure doesn’t. Anyways, since we can’t do this, thankfully we have our backup War Criminal to do our dirty work, so Michael asks Georgiou to help her, and they go AWOL.

Michael is legit the worst first officer I have ever seen.

Book’s cat Grudge is left behind, so now Tilly has to cat sit her. I want the episode to just be her wrangling this big ass cat as she crawls all over her. This also got one good laugh out of us. “Computer, locate Michael.” “She is not on board”. Tilly holds Grudge out and squints her eyes. “Did… did you eat her??”

Michael and Georgiou are on some shithole Orion Syndicate planet with a sadistic Geoffry like Orion who loves torturing his slaves. Book is enslaved by him, by the way. We get to watch a guy’s head explode! Modern Trek REALLY wants to Game of Thrones. They all work together to start a prison break, Book with his new Andorian friend he made in the prison. This Andorian is so dead.

Gah damn, that did not last long. They were really building that up. THough actually it’s a fakeout, he DID jump in front a bullet to save Booker, but he’s rescued by Georgiou and Michael before he can bleed out. Meanwhile, Georgiou is having some seizures or something.

Stamets and Adira bond over having dead boyfriends who’s souls kinda hung onto them. It’s a weird but touching scene.

Booker and Michael make out in the turbolift as she’s about to go get chewed out by Saru for insubordination. Does she have… a kink?? She ALSO gets chewed out by the Admiral. “Permission to speak, sir?” “Well, it better be the best thing I’ve ever heard.” It will be, because its Michael saying it. This series is basically a bunch of scenes of Michael saying a thing, others saying “no”, then her repeating exactly what she just said and them going “you know what you’re right”. They keep harping on that yes, she did a bad, but hey her intel was good and she saved lives. Saru also demotes her, which is a long time coming tbh.

This was annoying.

Unification III - DIS 3/10

HEY, Y’ALL REMEMBER UNIFICATION I AND II? WE’RE BACK TO THAT I GUESS. That was like TWENTY YEARS before this.

Anyways you know how the admiral has been like, multiple times, “we are uninterested in learning more about what happened to the Burn”? Well Michael gets more information and he changes his opinion. They need a thing though, from Ni’Var, AKA Vulcan. See, the unification succeeded and now it’s a Vulcan/Romulan planet. Spock succeeded, yay. But Ni’Var left the Federation after the Burn, believing through twisted logic the Federation did it. Once Michael learns that they left the Federation, she IMMEDIATELY becomes racist about the Romulans.

Turns out uh, no. Logic Extremists. You know how it is. I hate Modern Trek Vulcans. Anyway, even though Michael was insubordinate and demoted and everyone is angry at her, she’s chosen to be an ambassador to Ni’Var to try and get information from them and share the info she learned about the Burn. Sure.

THEY WATCH A RECORDING OF UNIFICATION I. DID PICARD RECORD SPOCK IN THAT CAVE?!

TILLY IS PROMOTED TO XO??? Good on her.

The Vulcans refuse to give them the data they require, so Michael invokes some ANCIENT VULCAN RITUAL that makes it so she can not be denied. Kind of… weird, but okay. None of the Vulcans are happy at her doing this and are of course rude, snooty, and racist. Lovely. They also give her an advocate, a member of the Qowat Milat. REMEMBER THEM, FROM PICARD? Also turns out she’s HER MOM!! Wow, how… coincidental!

Anyways, what proceeds is a court episode. Some of my favorite kinds of episodes! Unfortunately, most court episodes aren’t full of… whatever the fuck is going on with Vulcan politics right now. There are three people judging this. One is a Vulcan “purist”, AKA a racist. Another is a Romulan. And the last is a Vulcan-Romulan hybrid. All three are advocating namely for their own peoples and purposes, and are at odds. Mostly, the Romulan and the Vulcan are at odds, while the vulco-romulan abstains.

Her mom also kind of torpedos her chances by y’know, sticking to absolute candor, making sure everyone knows about her insurbodination and that she can’t really be trusted. Everyone in the room is subjected to watching a spat between a mother and a daughter and Michael crash out because she doesn’t know if she belongs in the Federation anymore. They are being forced to be witness to this. I’d be annoyed.

She almost causes a cultural schism between the Romulans and the Vulcans, but then fixes it by making some grand statement about how it’s not what Spock would have wanted. She ends up withdrawing her request for the data so it doesn’t cause a further schism. This, of course, gets them to give her the data. They ALSO are like “I wonder how much of who Spock became is because of Michael.” MICHAEL SURE IS THE SPECIAL BOY, HUH?

Tilly decides to be an XO and Michael decides to stay here, for “the duration”. Or as long as it takes for her to decide everyone is wrong and go rogue again.

Saru makes moves on the Vulcan president, who seems into it. Saru can get it.

The Sanctuary - DIS 4/10

Booker’s home planet is basically under attack by the Emerald Chain, the modern Orion Syndicate. So they ask the Admiral so send them to fix it. He says no. Michael asks, again. He says yes. Once you notice it happens so much its EXTREMELY distracting. We also meet the ruler of the Emerald Chain, who murders her nephew in a very Game of Thrones scene.

Tilly is following Saru around filling out his schedule. Imagine if we saw Riker do that for Picard. They do know XO isn’t secretary, right?

Woke? Adira comes out as nonbinary to Stamets who’s like “aight.” I like Gay Dad Stamets. And yeah, thats about how it’d happen. I already knew about this, for the record, because my dad complained at me five years ago about how woke Star Trek was being. Anyways Stamets and Adira bond more over playing music together. Adira can’t seem to contact their boyfriend and it’s bothering them, and Stamets distracts them with the music. I LOVE Gay Dad Stamets.

We have… too many plotlines moving at once. We’re on the planet meeting Booker’s brother and learning more about him and his people, and also Georgiou is having more episodes and being looked at by the doctors, AND the leader of the Emerald Chain is trying to coerce them into doing what she wants. Her name is Osyraa.

At least those two last things combine together, we learn that Osyraa is forcing Book’s brother to betray them. She wants Book, since he was her slave, and she wants Burnham now so she has leverage over the Federation.

Osyraa fires upon the planet, apparently these are photon torpedos exploding behind them? If they were they’d be vaporized. The Federation can’t go to war, so they send a rogue agent who’s totally going against rules, using Booker’s ship. Detmer goes with the Andorian from the other episode and attacks her ship. Also apparently this Andorian is the only person who’s ever stood up to Osyraa, which is why she wants him so bad. The ONLY person? She rules an immoral slave empire. Anyways we get a Star Wars scene, and she’s not buying their excuses, so she declares war. What a surprise. Just… blow her up?

The Emerald Chain leaves, and Michael solves the problem this planet has had for decades that they were relying on the Emerald Chain to fix. She solves it instantly. Cool.

ONCE YOU REALIZE IT HAPPENS EVERY EPISODE, IT IS VERY, VERY DISTRACTING.

Anyways the two brothers do the thing and save the day, and fix their problems.

We also find out WHY Osyraa actually wants Ryn, the Andorian. He’s the only one who knows the Chain is running out of Dilithium….. you mean THE THING EVERYONE IS RUNNING OUT OF?! NO FUCKING WAY, REALLY?!

Booker decides to join Starfleet, yay. The end.

Terra Firma, Part 1 - DIS 3.5/10

Georgiou is literally falling apart dimensionally. Apparently she has dimensional sickness from time travel AND dimension travel, which is bad I guess. They use the sphere data and find a cure. Also apparently off screen the sphere data merged with the computer and formed an AI. We saw it talking but they never… drew attention to it being a thing.

Anyways the Admiral was like “if you let her die, your crew will never look at you the same way again for letting a fellow crewmember die.” DUDE. SHE’S AN UNLIKABLE MURDERER. She literally ate sapient people.

I don’t know why they’re trying to make me like her. Michael goes to offer her help and she tries to kill her. THIS is our beloved crewmember??? She goes down to the planet and everyone tearfully hugs her and wishes her well, saying it was an honor. I…. dude. This is dumb. This could have been handled so much better if Georgiou wasn’t CONSTANTLY the worst person and showing no signs of being better in any way. If she was a Terran Grunt learning to be better this’d be fine, but she’s still evil as shit.

They go down to a snowy planet and find some guy sitting, smoking a cigar in the middle of a snow field. He introduces himself as Carl. He has a door just standing there, and is like “welp, go on through”. They don’t trust him. I trust him implicitely, cause he likes puns.

Meanwhile, we triangulate the SOS signal from the source of the burn. The ship is still sending out that SOS so it’s still functional somehow, even 150 years later.

Georgiou goes through the door and finds herself back in time, AND in her own universe. She’s there the day where Lorca and Michael attempted to kill her. So she’s going to change things, kill Lorca, and “return Michael to the fold”. I dunno how no one doesn’t notice she’s like, 10 years older.

You can see that her time in the Prime Universe has, in fact, changed her. She feels kind of bad about the Kelpien slaves they have. She saves Saru’s life. I kinda wish we had… SEEN this evolution through the entire series, instead of just now.

There’s something about this… so, Modern Trek is filled with violence and people acting nuts and evil for no reason, which means that the Mirror Universe isn’t like, a shocking thing, it’s mostly annoying.

It also seems to be addicted with the idea that fascism is cool and powerful.

Georgiou kills her would be assassin, Stamets, with no problem, and confronts Michael about her assassination attempt. Mirror Michael is… nuts, cackling about how Lorca loves her for her and totally isn’t grooming her, and Georgiou decides not to kill her but instead throw her in the agonizer. What a surprise.

Terra Firma, Part 2 - DIS 3/10

This episode does that thing where they change the intro for a mirror episode, like they did in enterprise. But instead of a cool unique thing like in Enterprise, it’s uh, just mirrored. And upside down. That’s a little more lazy.

Michael is tortured nearly to death, but Georgiou is SURE she can reform her, so doesn’t kill her. This weirds everyone out. Also Lorca isn’t coming, of course. Dude got what he needed.

She eventually breaks and swears to kill all of her co-conspirators, alongside Detmer. Detmer, notably, was ALSO a co-conspirator, so I dunno what SHE gets out of this. She is also eventually killed.

She also makes some changes. She stops other problems that were threatening the empire. She makes the Kelpiens… suffer less under her rule. Everyone suffers less. The Terrans are also weirded out by this. You know what this is?

This is an Isekai episode.

She enters into a story with knowledge of it and uses that to make the perfect story she always wanted. It’s an Isekai.

Michael is playing the long game, and build ANOTHER rebellion, everyone turning on the Emperor. Except for… THE KELPIENS! Yes, turns out not treating them like meat will make them protect you. Michael and Georgiou kill each other and bleed out next to each other. The coup… failed? Or succeeded???

Georgiou reawakens in front of Carl and Michael. We also find out that Carl is THE GUARDIAN OF FOREVER…. remember him? He was the guy from one of the best TOS episodes. I dunno if this really… holds up to that history, but that’s fine. He explains he’s been in hiding cause everyone tried to use him to kill people in the temporal wars. He was testing her to make sure she wasn’t going to kill people, basically.

I kinda like Carl being the Guardian of Forever tbh. He’s kinda fun, and his avatar just being a shmuck in a bowler hat is fun too.

Georgiou is like “I wish I had learned how to not be evil earlier…” Well, people tried, but you kept threatening to put their heads on spikes and shit. Maybe if we had a better show we could actually have seen you growing and being a better character but instead character growth is shotgun blasted right at the fucking end here. Michael and Georgiou say goodbye to each other, and she heads off into the Guardian of Forever. Goodbye, Georgiou. You were… a SERIOUS waste of a character.

Admiral: “My condolences. We all feel her absense.” ???????????????

A toast! To Displaced Space Hitler! The greatest crewmate you could ever imagine. They go REALLY hard on this. The stuff earlier was hitting this uh, this is NOT hitting.

SHE WAS SUCH A GIRLBOSS. Fucking AIRAM hit harder than this, and she had had like 5 words.

It fucking ends on that. Christ, I was LIKING this episode until that point. She did not earn that. SHE REALLY DID NOT. WE SAW HOW SHE INTERRACTED WITH EVERYONE IN EVERY EPISODE SHE WAS IN. YOU CAN’T FUCKING PISS IN MY MOUTH AND TELL ME ITS RAINING. I DON’T CARE HOW MUCH SHE SAVED ONE KELPIEN IN ANOTHER TIMELINE.

entry.title: LizstarTrek - Discovery Season 3 episodes 1 - 5
entry.content:
Every Sunday my Twitch subs and I watch Star Trek in my Discord. Here are my reviews and thoughts on each of the episodes as I see it. If you’re curious about a nerd’s views on Star Trek episodes, please read on, I go quite in depth with some of these episodes! I’ve watched some Star Trek before but not all of it!
